## 1. The Invisible Hand
Have you ever wondered why a rolling ball eventually comes to a stop, or why you don't just float away into the sky? Every single day, invisible pushes and pulls are happening all around you, controlling everything. Let's explore this mystery!

Imagine you are standing in front of a heavy box. What exactly do you have to do to make it move forward? What would happen if your friend pushes it from the opposite side at the exact same time? Take a guess before moving on.

content.title: Visualizing Pushes and Pulls
content.description: An abstract visualization of a push and a pull.

content: In science, a push or a pull on an object is called a **Force**. Forces can change the state of motion of an object (make it move, stop, or change direction) or even change its shape.
Remember, a force always involves an interaction between at least two objects. No interaction means no force!
Many students think objects stop moving because they 'run out' of force. Actually, they stop because of an invisible force called friction pushing against them!

question: What happens when two equal forces act on an object in opposite directions?
options: The net force becomes zero and the object does not change its state of motion.
The object moves in the direction of the first force.

content: Take a moment to reflect: Explain to a friend or younger sibling how opening a door and kicking a football both involve the same scientific concept, even though they look completely different.

Force connects to everything in physics! It is the fundamental prerequisite for understanding Work and Energy, and it explains real-world phenomena like Friction (why shoes wear out) and Gravity (why apples fall from trees).

Mini Challenge: Find a rubber band. Stretch it to change its shape. Then, push a book across your table to change its motion. You just applied forces in two different ways! Can you identify which was a push and which was a pull?
